reason: WRONG ANSWER KEY: correct_option_id was 'b' (m²·K/W = R-value units). W/(m·K) is the correct unit for thermal conductivity (k-value). Also added missing rationale entry for option 'a'.

rationale.a: W/(m·K) is the correct SI unit for thermal conductivity (k-value), representing heat flow per unit length per degree of temperature difference.
rationale.b: m²·K/W is R-value (thermal resistance), which depends on thickness — not thermal conductivity.
rationale.c: Btu·in/(hr·ft²·°F) is imperial k-value; correct units but less commonly used in metric regions.
rationale.d: Degrees per watt is not a recognized unit for thermal conductivity.
rationale.correct: k-value is thermal conductivity in W/(m·K) per ASTM C518; it describes material's ability to conduct heat, independent of thickness.
rationale.takeaway: k = thermal conductivity (material property, independent of thickness). R = thermal resistance (depends on thickness and k).
